items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: I see Al Hibbler. I had forgotten I had recorded with him. That was on Aladdin.

ctx.x: I beg your pardon. It was at 7000 Santa Monica, certainly -- at the corner of Orange and Santa Monica or something like that. This was the same place where we did Benny Goodman's records, in the same studio. Val Valentin was the engineer there at the time. I really liked Val because he used to always get a good sound on the bass. He wasn't afraid if the meter moved a little bit. See, that was one of the fastest records ever made, and he beat it off ONE-TWO, ONE-TWO, ONE-TWO-THREE-FOUR, and there he'd go. Red…

I had forgotten another Erroll Garner record when he was recording for Mercury. "Blue Skies," "Don't Blame Me," "Full Moon and Empty Arms" and "Memories Of You". What brings that to mind is Milt Holland played drums on that. That was the first time I had ever worked with Milt Holland.
